Folks — attached is the quick worksheet (spreadsheet attached as acme-capacity-estimate-20270304.xlsx). Summary here so Sanjay can see numbers in-thread: 

Agent streaming (target: 95th <= 400ms, concurrency 50):
- Typical single-turn avg tokens in/out: 120 tokens in prompt, 180 tokens out (avg).
- Effective tokens/sec per connection during streaming: ~650 tokens/sec (typical chunking + network overhead).
- Sustained qps equivalent: 50 concurrent * (responses per minute ~ 1.2) -> ~1 QPS steady for the flow, but streaming concurrency drives concurrent GPU memory & KV cache requirements.
- Peak short bursts we saw in demos: 50 concurrent with simultaneous long responses — recommend provisioning for 2x the observed streaming bandwidth for burst headroom.
- Recommendation: Dedicated pool of 1 x 80GB GPU (A100-80GB class or equivalent) with model quantization to int8 and inference config tuned for streaming. This target gives headroom for 50 concurrent streaming sessions with 95th latency budget ~350ms in our tests. Add a 30% capacity buffer for safe estimates.

Batch summarization (target: tolerant of 30s latency, sustained 12 QPS, bursts to 60 QPS for ~3 minutes):
- Typical job request size: 8k tokens input, 1k tokens output (summarization).
- Sustained throughput: 12 QPS equates to ~96k tokens/sec system-wide; bursts to 60 QPS ~480k tokens/sec for short windows.
- Recommendation: For the batch window, use a Dedicated autoscaling group sized to 2 x A40-equivalent GPUs to hit the steady+burst profile with job-level batching and queueing. If using Hosted, expect throttling during burst windows unless you accept degraded latency; we can provide burst credit options but SLA guarantees require Dedicated.

Operational notes:
- Enable KV prefix caching for Agent chat to reduce repeated prompt tokens on multi-turn sessions.
- Use request-level quotas and soft-rate limits on client side to avoid sudden full-cluster bursts from scheduled cron jobs.
- Suggest a fallback model (smaller family) for non-critical summarization tasks to reduce peak cost.
